_note: Source-grounded entry for EQUIDERMA AI. Unsupported fields are intentionally null or empty.
description: A common chronic or relapsing inflammatory dermatitis affecting sebaceous-gland-rich areas, especially the scalp, face, and trunk.
symptoms: Mild or absent itch in many cases
Scalp dandruff may be asymptomatic or mildly itchy
causes: The cause is not completely understood.
Malassezia yeast proliferation is believed to contribute to inflammation.
risk_factors: Stress or lack of sleep may precipitate flares
Some neurologic conditions and medications are associated

appearance.general: Ill-defined scaly patches or diffuse scale, often with yellowish/greasy or white bran-like scale; common sites include scalp, eyebrows, nasolabial folds, ears, sternum, and skin folds.
appearance.dark_skin: Darker skin may show scaly hypopigmented macules and patches; children with skin of colour may show erythema, flaking, and hypopigmentation rather than classic cradle-cap appearance.

warning_signs: Extensive disease or suspected secondary bacterial or fungal infection should be medically assessed.
prevention: Identify and reduce factors that trigger flares when possible.
doctor_discussion_points: Discuss the distribution and recurrence of the rash.
Discuss whether another diagnosis such as psoriasis, tinea, or contact dermatitis needs consideration.
